title: Packing binary records
description:
Pack records into bytes with `string.pack` and read them back.

```
packed 3 records into 25 bytes
1  Ada      91
2  Bob      48
3  Céline   77
checksum: 0x0D
```

starter.main.lua:
local records = { { 1, "Ada", 91 }, { 2, "Bob", 48 }, { 3, "Céline", 77 } }
local parts = {}
for _, r in ipairs(records) do
  -- TODO: string.pack("<I2s1B", ...)
end
local data = table.concat(parts)
print("packed " .. #records .. " records into " .. #data .. " bytes")

hints: `local id, name, score, pos = string.unpack("<I2s1B", data, pos)` gives the next position to read from (lesson 7.03).
`for i = 1, #data do sum = sum ~ data:byte(i) end`.
requirements: Each record is `<I2 s1 B`: a little-endian 16-bit id, a name with a 1-byte length, and a score byte.
Unpack with `string.unpack` in a loop, using the position it returns.
A checksum is the XOR of every byte, worked out with `~` (Lua's bitwise xor).
stretch: Add a header with a magic string and a record count, and refuse data with the wrong magic.
